title: Fire-Flyer AI-HPC: A Cost-Effective Software-Hardware Co-Design for Deep Learning
problem: High costs of HPC construction due to expensive computing chips and interconnects, combined with exponentially increasing computational demands from Deep Learning and Large Language Models.
motivation: Cost-effective AI-HPC infrastructure is essential for enabling widespread adoption and sustainability of large-scale AI workloads.
method: Fire-Flyer 2 combines hardware and software design to reduce HPC costs: it uses 10,000 PCIe A100 GPUs connected via HFReduce (an optimized way for GPUs to combine their results) and a Computation-Storage Integrated Network that prevents data traffic bottlenecks. The software stack (HaiScale, 3FS, HAI-Platform) lets computation and data transfer happen simultaneously instead of waiting for each to finish. Together, these achieve performance comparable to expensive DGX-A100 systems while costing 50% less and using 40% less energy.
key_novelty: The key insight is co-designing hardware and software as one system: optimized GPU-to-GPU communication combined with a bottleneck-free network cuts costs 50% while matching expensive standard systems.
contributions: Fire-Flyer 2 architecture achieving 50% cost reduction and 40% energy efficiency improvement over DGX-A100
HFReduce mechanism for accelerating allreduce collective communication
Software stack enabling computation-communication overlap for scalability
System design insights for cost-effective large-scale AI-HPC deployment
